info.title: Dazzle.net
info.subtitle: DSSSL for .NET: the packages, the extensions, readings of the standard, and the parts of it they have

preface.title: About this document
preface.para: Dazzle.net runs DSSSL stylesheets (ISO/IEC 10179:1996) over SGML and XML documents on .NET (github.com/rschleitzer/dazzle-net). It builds on the C# port of James Clark's OpenSP and OpenJade (the packages OpenSP and OpenJade, github.com/rschleitzer/openjade-net) and adds a flow object class for writing directory trees and a PDF backend that sets the pages itself.

This document says what Dazzle.net adds to the standard, where it reads the standard in a way the standard leaves open, where it deviates, and which of the standard's optional parts it has. What the standard itself says is not repeated here; the clause numbers refer to ISO/IEC 10179:1996.

Every addition is made the way the standard provides for it: a flow object class with declare-flow-object-class, a characteristic with declare-characteristic, each with a public identifier of the form UNREGISTERED::Dazzle//…. A stylesheet that uses one declares it; another DSSSL engine reads such a stylesheet and passes the addition over.

chapter.title: The packages

row.entry: the command-line tool dazzle (-t sgml, -t xml, -t pdf), with the DTDs of the DSSSL architecture and a catalog for them
the PDF backend as a library, written with PDFsharp
the transformation backend with the directory flow object class

chapter.para: All target .NET 10. The tool is installed with dotnet tool install -g Dazzle.Cli:
chapter.programlisting: dazzle [options] DSSSL-spec document -t type output type: sgml, xml, pdf -o file output file -d spec DSSSL specification -V var define a variable -c catalog use an SGML catalog
chapter.para: From a program, Dazzle.Pdf sets a document with DssslProcessor:

A further overload of GeneratePdf writes to a Stream. Every call takes an optional path to an SGML catalog; without one the bundled catalog is used. An error in the document, the stylesheet or the formatting throws DssslProcessingException with the messages and their places ().
The fonts come from PDFsharp's font resolver: the one the program sets in GlobalFontSettings.FontResolver, else the fonts of the system.

section.title: The directory flow object class
section.para: The transformation backend writes text files through the entity flow object class. directory creates a directory and makes the entities inside it relative to it, so a stylesheet can lay out a whole tree of generated files.
section.programlisting:
(declare-flow-object-class entity "UNREGISTERED::James Clark//Flow Object Class::entity") (declare-flow-object-class directory "UNREGISTERED::Dazzle//Flow Object Class::directory")
(make directory path: "generated" (make entity system-id: "Parser.cs" (literal "// ...")))
section.para: In the package Dazzle and the tool. The C++ original modified for it and its port to Scaly (github.com/rschleitzer/dazzle) have it too.

section.title: Row heights: min-row-height and row-height
section.para: DSSSL has no height for a table row. Dazzle.Pdf takes it as two characteristics, specified on a table-row or anything around it.

row.entry: the row is at least this high
the row is exactly this high (0pt: as its cells ask)

section.para: The height belongs to the row and not to what is in it: OpenJade passes the style of a table-row on with its cells, and a table in a cell does not take on the height of the row around it (since 0.5.0). Since Dazzle.Pdf 0.2.0.

section.title: Columns: column-set and balance-columns?

note.para: Deprecated since Dazzle.Pdf 0.6.0: column-set-sequence with a column-set model () does the same in the terms of the standard. The two characteristics stay for one version.

section.para: DSSSL sets columns in the full page model (). Before Dazzle.Pdf had it, a display-group that specifies column-set set its content in columns.

row.entry: in points: the start of the first column from the start of the area and its width, then for every further column the gap before it and its width
the columns of the set's last page are made equally long

section.para: The set begins where the group begins, below the space before it. Content flows down a column into the next, from the last into the first column of the next page, and the set ends below its longest column. A paragraph's indents are measured from its column. At the top of a column conditional? space is dropped as at the top of a page. One column with an offset narrows the area. A balanced set ends at the smallest height at which the last column is not longer than the others; the first ones are rather the longer. A column set in a column set, a table cell, a header or a footer is an ordinary group.
Only the group that specifies column-set sets columns, not the flow objects in it, although an extension characteristic is inherited like any other. Since Dazzle.Pdf 0.4.0.

section.title: The first page: first-page-top-margin and first-page-bottom-margin

note.para: Deprecated since Dazzle.Pdf 0.6.0: a page-sequence with one page model for the first page and one for the others () does the same in the terms of the standard. The two characteristics stay for one version.

section.para: A simple-page-sequence has one set of margins. These two characteristics give its first page a top and a bottom margin of their own; 0pt means as the other pages.
Since Dazzle.Pdf 0.5.0.

section.title: An inline graphic beyond its line: grows-line?
section.para: An external-graphic set inline makes its line as tall as it needs, above the placement path as high as the graphic, below it as deep as its position-point-shift lowers it. With grows-line?: #f it leaves the line as its text and line spacing make it and reaches beyond, above or below, as a word processor draws a form field box that is taller than the reduced spacing of its line.

row.entry: whether an inline graphic makes its line taller

section.programlisting:
(declare-characteristic grows-line? "UNREGISTERED::Dazzle//Characteristic::grows-line?" #t)
(make sequence position-point-shift: -1.8pt grows-line?: #f (make external-graphic entity-system-id: "box.pdf" display?: #f))
section.para: Since Dazzle.Pdf 0.8.0.

section.title: Character spacing: letter-spacing
section.para: letter-spacing adds a length after every character of the text: also after the last character of a word, after a space and after the hyphen of a soft hyphen that breaks the line. A negative length narrows the text. The words are as much wider as they are drawn, so the line breaks where the spaced text ends, as a word processor's character spacing does.
Since Dazzle.Pdf 0.8.0.

section.title: Line heights as a word processor's: text-line-height, text-descent, line-height-factor
section.para: A line is as high as the tallest text in it needs, its placement path above the deepest descent, both from the fonts' metrics. Word processors give some fonts more than their metrics say (Word sets a line with MS Gothic 1.3 em high, of a font 1.0 em high), and measure every line of a paragraph for itself. text-line-height and text-descent give a text the height of a line and the part of it below the placement path that it needs, instead of its font's; 0pt, the initial value, is the font's. With line-height-factor not 0, every line of the paragraph is as high as its own text needs times the factor, in thousandths, and the rest beyond what the text needs lies below the placement path; line-spacing, min-leading, min-pre-line-spacing and min-post-line-spacing then do not count. At the end of an area the rest may lie past the end, as with min-post-line-spacing.

row.entry: the line height this text needs
how far this text needs to reach below the placement path
every line its own height times this, in thousandths

section.programlisting: (make paragraph line-height-factor: 1150 (make sequence font-family-name: "MS Gothic" text-line-height: 14.3pt text-descent: 3.17pt (literal "X")) (literal " a line in Arial Narrow"))
section.para: Since Dazzle.Pdf 0.10.0.

section.title: Squeezing justified lines: justify-squeeze, justify-squeeze-word, justify-squeeze-hyphen
section.para: A justified line breaks before the first word that does not fit, and its spaces are widened to fill it. Word processors also narrow the spaces to fit one more word: Word in its compatibility mode 15 lets a justified line run past the edge by a quarter of the width of each space between its words, but by no more than about a third of the word that does not fit together with the space before it, and narrows the spaces by as much; to break at a soft hyphen, by no more than about a third of the syllable before the hyphen. justify-squeeze gives the share of each space in thousandths of its width (0, the initial value, squeezes nothing), justify-squeeze-word the bound in thousandths of the word that does not fit, from the last space the line could break at (0: no such bound), and justify-squeeze-hyphen the bound at a soft hyphen in thousandths of the syllable before it, from the last place the line could break, the hyphen not counted (0: no such bound). Only a paragraph with quadding: 'justify squeezes.

row.entry: thousandths of a space each space may give
thousandths of the word that does not fit, at most
at a soft hyphen: thousandths of the syllable before it, at most

section.para: Since Dazzle.Pdf 0.11.0.

section.title: When a line breaks at a soft hyphen: hyphenation-ladder-count, hyphenation-zone, hyphenation-stretch, hyphenation-next-char?
section.para: Dazzle.Pdf does not hyphenate by itself: a stylesheet puts soft hyphens (U+00AD) into the text where a word may break, and a line breaks at the last of them that fits. Word processors are choosier, and these characteristics say when a soft hyphen that fits is taken. hyphenation-ladder-count is the one of ISO/IEC 10179: at most so many lines in a row end at a hyphen (#f, the initial value: any number). The others are extensions:

row.entry: A soft hyphen is taken only where
more room than this is left on the line before the word, from its start
that room is taken from the end of the word before, the space with it
the start indent of the line counts to that room
in a justified line instead of the zone: the line without the word would widen each of its spaces by more than so many thousandths of a space
the character after the hyphen would fit on the line as well

section.para: Word in its compatibility mode 14 takes a soft hyphen where more room than its hyphenation zone is left before the word, the indent of the line counted to it, and where the next character fits too; in mode 15 it ignores the zone of the document: in a ragged line it wants more than 18.26 points after the word before, in a justified line spaces widened by more than 0.49 of their width. Both limit the lines in a row that end at a hyphen.
section.programlisting: (make paragraph quadding: 'start hyphenation-ladder-count: 3 hyphenation-zone: 21.25pt hyphenation-zone-indent?: #t hyphenation-next-char?: #t (process-children))
section.para: Since Dazzle.Pdf 0.12.0; the bound of justify-squeeze-hyphen holds from the second syllable of a word on, the first is only bound by the spaces.

section.title: Where elements begin
section.para: Not a part of the language but of the program interface of Dazzle.Pdf: DssslProcessor.GeneratePdfWithLocations also says where each element with an ID (an attribute declared ID in the document's DTD) begins: the page, counted from 1, and the top left of the element's first line, or of the content of its table cell, in points from the top left of the page. A program that draws on the PDF afterwards can place things relative to an element.

The locations come from the marks the backend sets for every element processed in the initial processing mode, the same marks current-node-page-number-sosofo reads; an element processed only in a named mode has none. A mark has no height and holds no line. The top of a first line is below the element's space-before. Since Dazzle.Pdf 0.3.0.

chapter.title: What Dazzle.Pdf sets
chapter.para: Dazzle.Pdf sets the pages itself and writes them with PDFsharp: blocks flow down the page, paragraphs are broken into lines, tables are set row by row, and the flow object tree is laid out twice so that current-node-page-number-sosofo knows its page. That is enough to set a book with the DocBook print stylesheets.

listitem.para: simple-page-sequence with its header and footer parts, page-sequence and column-set-sequence ();
display-group, paragraph, paragraph-break, sequence, scroll;
line-field, leader, score, box, rule, external-graphic (a bitmap, or a PDF whose first page is drawn as a vector form; inline it is raised or lowered by position-point-shift like text, since 0.8.0);
the page number of the current page and of the current node.

section.title: What it passes over
section.para: Outside the page model Dazzle.Pdf does what the other backends of Jade do with what they do not have: it passes it over, without a message.

listitem.para: A flow object of a class it does not set shows its content as a sequence would, in the place where it stands: link (no link in the PDF), marginalia and sideline (in the text, not beside it), multi-mode, the math classes and grid.
alignment-point, formatting-instruction and the flow object classes of extensions other than its own set nothing.

Characteristics it does not read keep their value without effect. Among them: hyphenate? (a line breaks only where the text has a space or a hyphen, ), widow-count, orphan-count, keep, keep-with-previous? (only keep-with-next? holds a block to the next), may-violate-keep-before?, may-violate-keep-after?, last-line-quadding, line-cap, line-join, box-type, box-corner-radius, kern?, ligature?, language and country.

section.para: In the page model it is the other way round: what lies outside the subset fails the run ().

chapter.title: Errors
chapter.para: An error in a stylesheet fails the run, with the place in the stylesheet where it is: a characteristic with a value it cannot take, a form the engine does not have, a part of the page model outside the subset (). The C++ original reports these through its messenger; until OpenJade 1.4.0 the C# port wrote them to the console and went on, and Dazzle.Pdf set the document anyway.

Dazzle.Pdf adds the errors of what it cannot set although the language allows it, and fails the run with them as well: a column-set-sequence in a table cell, a header or a footer; a flow object in a column set with a span other than 1; a page of a page-sequence for which there is no page model.

chapter.title: Readings of the standard
chapter.para: Where the standard is silent or leaves a choice, Dazzle.Pdf decides as follows. The characteristics otherwise mean what ISO/IEC 10179 says, as the RTF backend of Jade has them.

listitem.para: A deviation: the initial value of input-whitespace-treatment is 'collapse, not 'preserve.

The spaces where a line is broken for its width stay at the end of that line, also under 'preserve, and do not indent the next one. The standard does not say where kept spaces go at a break; Dazzle.Pdf does what XSL's suppress-at-line-break describes and what word processors do (since 0.4.0).
A tab goes to the next multiple of 36pt.
line-spacing is the distance of the lines: exactly that with min-leading: #f (the initial value), otherwise at least that and the height of the line's text plus min-leading.

Below the placement path of a line is the descent of its text, or min-post-line-spacing where that is more; the rest of the line spacing is above (since 0.4.0; before, the characteristic had no effect). With min-pre-line-spacing alone, that much is above the placement path and the rest of the line spacing below (since 0.7.0).

A reading: a line area is min-pre-line-spacing before and min-post-line-spacing after its placement path, and the line spacing beyond that is space between lines (12.6.6.1). At the end of an area the last line therefore needs only its extent down to the descent of its text; the rest of min-post-line-spacing may lie past the end. Word processors do the same with the extra of a multiple line spacing; a line of exact height, whose space below the path is the rest of its line spacing, has to fit whole (since 0.7.0).

A line breaks at a space, after a soft hyphen (which then shows) and after a hyphen between letters, also where the letters are in different runs. A line breaks only once it holds something: a first word wider than the line overflows it.
Under 'preserve, where lines: 'wrap wraps a line it still breaks at the kept spaces.

section.title: Dashed lines: line-dash
section.para: A rule, a border of a table or of a table cell and a score are drawn with the line-dash in effect where they are made. As the standard has it, the first length of the list is the number component of the CurrentDashPattern of ISO/IEC 10180, the offset into the pattern at which the line starts, and the others are its vector component, alternately the lengths of dashes and gaps, as the arguments of PostScript's setdash; the initial value (0pt) is a solid line. A pattern of odd length repeats with dashes and gaps alternating, as in PostScript.
Since Dazzle.Pdf 0.9.0, with OpenJade 1.5.0, which passes the characteristic to the backend; the original installs it and ignores it.

section.title: Space between blocks
section.para: Display space collapses to the larger of the space after one block and the space before the next. conditional? space is dropped at the start of an area: the top of a page, of a column, of a table cell.

section.title: Breaks and keeps
section.para: break-before: 'column and break-after: 'column go on in the next column of a column set; outside one there is one column, and they go on on a new page (since 0.4.0). A set to be balanced that has a column break on its last page is not balanced: the explicit break wins.
keep-with-next?: #t holds a block on the page of the block after it; a run of such blocks moves to the next page together, as does a table row that does not fit.

listitem.para: The cell margins are the distance between the edges of a cell and its content.
A cell is placed in the column after the previous cell of its row unless its column-number says otherwise, also under a cell spanning rows.
The backgrounds of table cells lie under the contents and borders of every table on the page (since 0.3.1).
A table row is as high as its cells ask, unless min-row-height or row-height say more ().

section.title: Score and line fields
section.para: score draws its line after ('after), through or before the text, or at a length below it, over the spaces only with score-spaces?: #t. A line field in a score is scored over its whole width (since 0.3.1).

section.title: Headers and footers
section.para: The header and footer parts of a simple-page-sequence are set as blocks across the width of the page body, the center- and right- parts aligned to the middle and the end. They stand at header-margin from the top and footer-margin from the bottom of the page, and without these in the middle of the margin.

section.title: External graphics
section.para: scale: 'max-uniform (the initial value) is the largest uniform scale within max-width and max-height, 'max each direction on its own, numbers as they are. A graphic may overflow its line (since 0.3.1).

chapter.title: The page model
chapter.para: The standard divides the full page model into features (12.1): page allows the page-sequence and column-set-sequence flow object classes, multi-column column sets of more than one column, nested-column-set a column set within a column set. Dazzle.Pdf has page and multi-column, both restricted as below, and not nested-column-set (since 0.6.0, on OpenJade 1.4.0).

The C++ original reads define-page-model and define-column-set-model and skips them, and has neither flow object class. The C# port of OpenJade takes them as an addition of its own (src/OpenJade/Style/PageModel.cs) and gives the backend the models through FOTBuilder.
chapter.programlisting:
(define-page-model first (width 595pt) (height 842pt) (region (x-origin 70pt) (y-origin 56pt) (width 469pt) (height 600pt))) (define-page-model other (width 595pt) (height 842pt) (region (x-origin 70pt) (y-origin 56pt) (width 469pt) (height 730pt))) (define-column-set-model two (column-subset (column (x-origin 0pt) (width 220pt)) (column (x-origin 249pt) (width 220pt)) (balance? #t)))
(root (make page-sequence initial-page-models: (list first) repeat-page-models: (list other) (process-children))) (element section (make column-set-sequence column-set-model: two (process-children)))
chapter.para: Whatever lies outside the subset is an error at its place in the stylesheet; a characteristic outside it is allowed only with its initial value. Unlike elsewhere (), nothing of the page model is passed over silently: a page set on another geometry than the stylesheet asks for would go unnoticed.

row.entry: required: the size of the page
x-origin, y-origin, width, height of the region
required; the origin is at the lower left and y goes up (12.3.1), so y-origin is the bottom margin

section.title: The page-sequence flow object class (12.6.4)
section.para: initial-page-models and repeat-page-models are lists of page models. force-last-page, force-first-page, first-page-type, blank-back-page-model, blank-front-page-model, justify-spread?, binding-edge and page-category take their initial values only.

A reading: the standard says only that the models are used for the initial pages and for the pages after them. In Dazzle.Pdf the k-th page takes the k-th model of initial-page-models, and the pages after them go round repeat-page-models. More pages than models with an empty repeat-page-models are an error: there shall be an applicable page model for every page.
Like a simple-page-sequence, a page-sequence is a child of the root. Both may be used in one document.

section.title: The column-set-sequence flow object class (12.6.5)
section.para: column-set-model is required and not #f; column-set-model-map is empty only. space-before, space-after, keep-with-previous? and keep-with-next? are as on a display-group; break-before and break-after take 'page, 'column and #f. span, span-weak?, position-preference, keep, may-violate-keep-before? and may-violate-keep-after? take their initial values only. A column-set-sequence within a column-set-sequence is an error.

row.entry: one or more, each with x-origin and width (required for 'top-to-bottom by [218]), from the left edge of the column set
yes; an explicit column break in the last column set wins over it
#f only: the set ends below its longest column
allowed; without it the width of the area around

tie, further subsets, the zones top-float, bottom-float, footnote, justify?, justify-limit, justify-last-limit, length-decrease-order, align-lines?, top-float-space-below, bottom-float-space-above, height, decorate, headers, footers and footnote separators of columns

section.title: Models that depend on the document
section.para: Page and column-set models are top-level definitions, and the standard does not say what current-node or current-root return in them; a model cannot read its margins from the document. Where the geometry comes with the document, the program that calls Dazzle writes the models into a style specification of their own and takes the rules from the fixed stylesheet with the means the standard has for it, external-specification and use.
